title: Uniqueness of an adjunction with a fixed representative Hom formula
statement: Let C,D,H,J be arbitrary categories, T:C→D and U:D→C with adjunction b:T⊣U, Q:C→H and P:D→J, L:H→J and R:J→H. Fix natural transformations ε:Q⋙L→T⋙P and β:U⋙Q→P⋙R and a morphism property W on D. Assume P localizes W and R⋙L is right derived from U⋙Q⋙L with unit β whiskered by L followed by the associator. If adjunctions a,a′:L⊣R both satisfy a.homEquiv(QM,PK)(ε_M;P(t))=Q(b.homEquiv(M,K)(t));β_K for all M,K,t:T(M)→K, then a=a′. No abelian or scheme assumptions are required.

source.place: Tag 09T5 (derived adjunctions and universal properties); cohomology.tex Tag 06YJ (derived pullback). The normalization-uniqueness calculation is supplied explicitly by F2.

proof.text: Apply each Hom formula to t=b.counit_K at M=U(K). The underived right triangle identity says its transpose is identity. Applying inverse transposition gives L(β_K);a.counit_(PK)=ε_(UK);P(b.counit_K), and the same equation for a′.

These equations say the two counits have equal precomposition with the specified unit for R⋙L. Use the right-derived universal property (rightDerived_ext) to equate the counit natural transformations, then Adjunction.ext_counit to equate the adjunctions.

proof_origin.note: Explicit triangle-identity and right-derived-extensionality proof; no unproved auxiliary result added.
